body:
Always happy to see new debug/buffer previews!

I do have a few concerns though. I'm questioning the reasoning of altering the z-buffer this much from what Godot's z-buffer actually returns. In my experience, the purpose of these type of previews is to give the user an idea of what type of values they can expect when they read from a buffer, usually in the context of creating shaders (or when debugging), but in this case the preview
- Inverts the buffer
- Linearizes the buffer
- Makes the far plane a different color, which makes it seem like it's not part of the buffer or like its handled in some non-standard/different way.

This buffer preview communicates to the user that if we'd sample a nearby pixel, we'd get a near-black value, and a near-white value for a far away pixel, the opposite of what would actually happen. In my opinion, we should just show the raw result of `texture(depth_texture, SCREEN_UV).x`, without any changes. Otherwise I can only imagine this preview would become a source of confusion, and I'm not sure what purpose a buffer preview would serve if it's altered from what it actually returns.

Just for context, these are the values the user actually interfaces with when reading the depth buffer.
